learning_outcomes.text: define thermodynamic systems and perform energetic balancing
calculate thermodynamic state changes of ideal and real gases using the 1st and 2nd law of thermodynamics and analyze irreversibilities
calculate state variables in the two-phase region
name and describe the different thermodynamic cycles
investigate the process variables work and heat transfer in thermodynamic cycles and make statements about their efficiency based on this.

syllabus_topics: Thermodynamic equations of state for ideal and real gases
1st Law of Thermodynamics: Energy balancing, caloric equation of state, internal energy and enthalpy
Irreversible processes, closed systems in p-v and T-s diagrams, polytropic state changes of ideal gases
Homogeneous substances: vapor pressure curve, wet vapor region in p-v, T-s, and h-s diagrams, vapor quality
Thermodynamic cycles in the wet vapor region: Clausius-Rankine and vapor compression refrigeration cycle
Thermodynamic cycles with ideal gases: Carnot cycle, Stirling cycle, Otto cycle, Diesel cycle, Joule cycle
assessment_rules: Credit points are awarded upon successful completion of the module exam and submission of a study assignment (active participation in the exercises). The module grade's weight for the final grade is based on the credit points.
